metadata.name: 10kΩ Resistor
metadata.description: A generic 10kΩ resistor (0.25W) - commonly used for pull-down/pull-up configurations
metadata.author: Brendan Howell

connectionGuide.purpose: One end of the 10kΩ pull-down resistor. Used to keep a GPIO pin at a known LOW state when a button is not pressed.
warnings: This resistor prevents 'floating' inputs that cause unpredictable readings
Without a pull-down, a button circuit may read random HIGH/LOW values
troubleshooting: Resistors have no polarity - either end can connect to either side
If button readings are erratic, check that pull-down is properly connected to GND
10kΩ is a standard value - higher values use less power but are more noise-sensitive

connectionGuide.purpose: Other end of the 10kΩ pull-down resistor. One end connects to the GPIO pin (same bus as button), other end connects to GND.
warnings: For pull-DOWN: connect one end to GPIO bus, other end to GND
For pull-UP: connect one end to GPIO bus, other end to 3.3V
troubleshooting: Pull-DOWN circuit: Button connects GPIO to 3.3V when pressed, resistor pulls to GND when released
In code, button pressed = HIGH (1), button released = LOW (0)
If behavior is inverted, you may have a pull-UP configuration instead

warnings: Ensure power dissipation does not exceed 0.25W
At high temperatures, derate power rating
Common use: Pull-down or pull-up resistor for buttons/switches
